title: WebSeer: Training Deeper Search Agents through Reinforcement Learning with Self-Reflection
claim: Prior agents give up early or compound errors after a wrong step; ours cross-validates and self-reflects over many tool-use steps.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, red-error vs blue-success contrast with step boxes
description: The figure has two horizontal bands separated by a dashed line. The top band, labeled Search-r1, shows a Think → Local Search step feeding a dashed box of four numbered results. A relevant result leads to green Step 2 and Step 3 boxes. Step 3 then leads to an orange Give up box marked with a red X. An irrelevant result is labeled Wrong sub-answer and leads to orange Step 2, Step 3 and Answer boxes, also marked with an X. Annotations read Insufficient Search Depth and Error accumulation. The bottom band, labeled WebSeer, shows a large WebSeer module in Step 1 with Search, Read Webpage and Code runner tool boxes. It has Refine keywords, Cross-validation and Self-reflection feedback loops back to the agent. Step 2 shows WebSeer calling tools, followed by a wavy line labeled Up to 50 steps and a green Answer box with a blue check. Colors are blue, green and orange.
caption: Comparasion between different search agent: Search-r1[ref] faces shallow search and error buildup, while WebSeer trained using our self-reflection paradigm significantly improve tool calls and maintain rigorous reasoning.
abstract: Search agents have achieved significant advancements in enabling intelligent information retrieval and decision-making within interactive environments. Although reinforcement learning has been employed to train agentic models capable of more dynamic interactive retrieval, existing methods are limited by shallow tool-use depth and the accumulation of errors over multiple iterative interactions. In this paper, we present WebSeer, a more intelligent search agent trained via reinforcement learning enhanced with a self-reflection mechanism. Specifically, we construct a large dataset annotated with reflection patterns and design a two-stage training framework that unifies cold start and reinforcement learning within the self-reflection paradigm for real-world web-based environments, which enables the model to generate longer and more reflective tool-use trajectories. Our approach substantially extends tool-use chains and improves answer accuracy. Using a single 14B model, we achieve state-of-the-art results on HotpotQA and SimpleQA, with accuracies of 72.3% and 90.0%, respectively, and demonstrate strong generalization to out-of-distribution datasets. The code is available at https://github.com/99hgz/WebSeer
